A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Similarity-Dissimilarity Loss framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable, allowing relocated and renamed material to be matched.

before.justification: v5 reports original image-classification, AAPD text-classification, and MIMIC medical-coding experiments in Table 1 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v6 retains those original experiments and adds image-baseline comparisons, component ablations, and robustness results.

M1.justification: The proposed loss, similarity and dissimilarity factors, positive-set construction, and two-phase training procedure remain unchanged. Sim-Dissim renames Ours; the factor-removal variants are ablations of existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MS-COCO, PASCAL, NUS-WIDE, AAPD, and the same MIMIC-III/IV full-label and top-50 settings. The new analyses use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Jaccard (Lin et al., 2023), Class proto (Gupta et al., 2023), and MSC (Audibert et al., 2024) across all three image benchmarks, substantially broadening the previous ALL/ANY/MulSupCon comparison. AAPD and medical comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols toggle the two loss factors, partition MS-COCO into 23 head and 57 tail classes using cumulative training frequency, and evaluate batch sizes 32, 64, 128, and 256 on validation data. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, encoders, and stated training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v6 adds component ablations on MS-COCO and AAPD (Table 4), explicit head-versus-tail analysis (Figure 6), and batch-size sensitivity analysis (Figure 7). These directly investigate component contributions and robustness beyond v5's existing benchmark comparisons and discussion.

E5.justification: Figure 7 newly reports capped error bars for individual method/batch-size results. Their statistical meaning and underlying run counts are unspecified, so additional repeated runs cannot be inferred. The earlier cross-method dispersion plots remain.

E6.justification: v6 adds image-baseline scores, factor-ablation entries, and head/tail and batch-size results while retaining the earlier benchmark values. Newly evaluated Jaccard and MSC achieve PASCAL mAP of 80.09 and 80.02, respectively, exceeding Sim-Dissim's unchanged 79.75.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a proof for the existing label-equivalence/vector-similarity Lemma 1, invoking convergence and normalized representations. The five weighting-factor theorems and their proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims about multi-label relations, similarity-dissimilarity weighting, theoretical foundations, unified supervised contrastive loss, and cross-domain performance remain. Although the abstract drops its MIMIC-III-Full state-of-the-art sentence, corresponding claims persist in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets the factors as synergistic, attributes larger tail-label gains to suppressing weak positives, and argues robustness across batch sizes. The medical discussion adds calibration and metric-saturation explanations. The existing low-label-cardinality limitation remains.

D1.justification: The hardware and implementation settings are retained from v5 Appendix F in v6 Appendix C.4. However, v5's anonymous code-repository link in footnote 8 is removed, although v6 still directs readers to code for additional configuration details.

R1.justification: v6 adds Gupta et al. (2023) and discussion of class-prototype contrastive learning, adds Huang et al. (2025), and removes Huang et al. (2019). The principal positioning against overlap-based contrastive methods remains.

P1.justification: v6 substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative into separate image, text, medical, and ablation sections, incorporating former appendix material. It consolidates experimental setup appendices, edits prose throughout, and removes the separate ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: v6 changes the publication template and typography, expands Table 1, relocates existing AAPD and medical comparisons, and adds Table 4 and Figures 4–7. Figures 4–5 visualize retained medical results; Figures 6–7 display new analyses.

improvement.justification: Broader baselines and targeted analyses address gaps in v5, but the new supporting evidence has unresolved inconsistencies. Figure 6's 23 head classes scoring 75.31 and 57 tail classes scoring 57.61 imply overall macro-F1 of approximately 62.70, rather than the reported 70.03; no alternative aggregation is explained. Together with undefined new error bars, this limits confidence in the added robustness evidence and prevents a reliable net-quality judgment.
